_: THIS REPO'S OWN context budget — BL-37 half (a), provisioned by S90 (2026-08-15) from starter-kit/context-budget.json and then CALIBRATED, per that seed's own instruction to replace every inherited number with one defensible from a measurement of this project. This repo AUTHORS and DISTRIBUTES the FM #28 gate (bin/_manifest.py:54 ships starter-kit/context_budget.py -> adopter context_budget.py, :60 ships the seed -> adopter .context-budget.json) and until now had never configured it for itself — the same blind-at-home shape as BL-29 and upstream issue #59, arriving through configuration rather than path resolution. Run: python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py (there is no root copy of the tool here; see _tool_location below).
_tool_location: The tool is NOT at this repo's root. bin/_manifest.py installs it at ADOPTER roots; canonically it lives only at starter-kit/context_budget.py. Two consequences, both measured not assumed: (1) invoke it as `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py` — find_root() then walks up to this repo root via .git and reads this file, which is why a root-relative `path` below still resolves; (2) `install-hook` would write a hook that execs $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/context_budget.py, which does not exist here, AND this clone already sets core.hooksPath=.githooks whose pre-commit is the FM #27 ledger gate, so install-hook correctly declines with 'already exists and is not ours'. The budget gate is therefore MEASURING here, not BLOCKING. Wiring it into .githooks/pre-commit would edit a canonical file that ships upstream — deliberately not done here; raised as a follow-on instead.
_bytes_per_token: MEASURED ON THIS REPO, 2026-08-15 (S90). Regression of each session's opening context on the size of CLAUDE.md at that session's start, over n=75 transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-rmsharp-Development-methodology: opening_tokens ~= 42,033.2 + 0.356891 x bytes, R^2 = 0.8083 => 2.8020 B/tok, rounded here to 2.80. Corroborated by two independent local instruments: the same fit with only the lineage defect corrected gives 2.93 (R^2 = 0.6854), and the natural experiment across commit 7603f10 (CLAUDE.md 52,909 -> 8,519 B, -44,390 B) using the two sessions bracketing it within 20 minutes on each side gives 44,390 B / 17,616 tok = 2.52. Three local estimates spanning 2.52-2.93, and the seed's 2.93 from a different project, all agree within ~15%. THE TOOL NOW AGREES — BL-38 FIXED IT (S91, 2026-08-15). The warning that used to live in this key said `--calibrate` prints 14.45 B/tok at R^2 = 0.0513 and must not be adopted; that is no longer true and the key would otherwise have become a false claim about a tool that had been repaired. The two defects behind it (D1: `git log -- CLAUDE.md` walked ALL merged ancestry, so upstream's own CLAUDE.md lineage interleaved with this fork's by commit date and 'size at time T' stopped being a function; D2: ISO timestamps were sorted and compared AS STRINGS across mixed offsets) are fixed in starter-kit/context_budget.py. Re-run `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py --calibrate` rather than trusting this sentence: at n=76 it prints 2.81 B/tok at R^2 = 0.8054, against the 2.80 recorded here from S90's n=75. The small drift is the extra transcript, not a disagreement. A fit below R^2 = 0.50 is now REFUSED by the tool rather than printed, so this key can no longer be 'corrected' to noise by a session that reads the number and not the statistic.
_fixed_harness_tokens: MEASURED — the intercept of the same n=75 fit above: the opening context that exists before any budgeted file is loaded (system prompt, tool schemas, skill listings, MCP server tools, agent-level memory). The seed carries 35,700 from a different project and a different harness configuration; this repo's floor is higher. Note what this makes CLAUDE.md worth: at 11,064 B and 2.80 B/tok it is 3,951 tok, 9.4% of this floor.
_growth_run: INHERITED FROM THE SEED, NOT DERIVED — and labelled so rather than presented as measured. It cannot be calibrated on day one: this repo has no .context-budget-history.jsonl until this config's first run, so the series the trigger reads is empty. Revisit once ~15 measurements exist; the honest input is how many consecutive non-shrinking readings this repo actually produces between deliberate reductions (S23, S24, S25, S87 and S89 were all reductions, so the true run length here is probably short).

resident._: Resident is a ONE-FILE class in this repo — CLAUDE.md is the only artifact the harness injects in full before the session starts; this repo has no root SESSION_RUNNER.md (its runner is the distributed starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md) and no root SESSION_NOTES.md (its continuity record is HANDOFFS.md). So this total equals CLAUDE.md's own ceiling by construction. That is deliberate and it is NOT a check that cannot fail: the per-file ceiling cannot see a SECOND resident file being added, and this one can. Agent-level memory (~/.claude/projects/.../MEMORY.md) is genuinely resident too but is per-operator and per-machine, outside this repo, and not a reviewable diff — deliberately excluded, and worth remembering when reading the 42,033-tok floor above, which INCLUDES it.

structure.why: CLAUDE.md's own Versioning section states that this heading must stay put because existing CLAUDE.md#versioning links resolve to it; the v3.7-era extraction to docs/RELEASE_HISTORY.md kept the heading for exactly that reason. A compaction that removes it breaks frozen citations silently.

files._: max_lines 200 is THIS FRAMEWORK'S OWN PUBLISHED NUMBER, not an invention: starter-kit/BOOTSTRAP.md:199 says 'Claude Code targets roughly 200 lines' and tells adopters to extract to a referenced PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md before that budget is crowded. Dogfooding it here is the whole point of BL-37. max_bytes converts it at this file's measured density — 11,064 B / 119 lines = 92.97 B/line, x200 = 18,594 B, rounded to 18,600 — because a line ceiling alone just produces longer lines. warn_bytes sits 2,600 B below, which is two of the largest single-session increases this file has actually taken since the S24 cut (+1,308 B at d69f7a9, +1,017 B at 316e7ef), so the warning arrives with about two sessions of notice. NO protected_fence IS DECLARED, deliberately: the seed's budget:protected fence does not exist in this file, and declaring it without adding it would report 'over' for a missing fence — a red manufactured by this config rather than a real defect. Adding the fence edits canonical content that ships upstream; raised as a follow-on instead.

structure.why: the same anchor this ledger's own front-matter audit grep uses, and the same one methodology_trim.py's CHANGELOG LedgerSpec keys records on. If it stops matching, the file has been restructured and every size check here is measuring something else.

files._: Read-mandated: SESSION_RUNNER.md Phase 0 step 6 reconciles this file against git log every session, and Phase 3F writes to it. max_bytes 65,536 is NOT chosen here — it is starter-kit/methodology_trim.py:69 DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES = 64 * 1024, 'calibrated to the three sizes this repo operated at', the same ceiling BL-9/BL-32/BL-36/S87/S89 have all measured against. Cross-checked: `python3 starter-kit/methodology_trim.py --file CHANGELOG.md --check` reports 48,469 B against a 65,536 B budget, trigger does not fire — two independent tools, same verdict. max_lines 2,000 is the agent Read cap, a mechanically real ceiling this repo has already been bitten by: BL-9's L2 found this file had crossed it and was silently dropping its 10 oldest entries. NO max_line_bytes, deliberately — see HANDOFFS.md below, same reason.

structure.why: receipts are fenced blocks — the shape bin/check-handoff validates and methodology_trim.py's HANDOFFS LedgerSpec keys on (record_kind=fence, fence_info=handoff). Zero matches means the receipts are no longer receipts.

files._: Read-mandated: Phase 0 step 6 reconciles this file's frontier and Phase 3A reads the predecessor's receipt in full. max_lines 1,200 is THIS FILE'S OWN DECLARED TRIGGER, stated in its front matter ('Archive again ... when this one approaches ~1,200 lines'), which is tighter than the 2,000-line Read cap and so governs. MAX_BYTES 65,536 IS RETAINED BUT NO LONGER THE OPERATIVE GUARD, and S98 measured why. Across 81 transcripts of this repo (the measuring session excluded, heredoc bodies stripped, classified per PIPELINE so `git show f | grep x` counts once): the live root ledger was read WHOLE into a session's context exactly ONCE and read in PART 593 times -- median span 25 lines, largest ever requested 220, against a 452-line file. No read in the corpus asked for even half of it. So the whole-file ceiling guards a cost paid once in 81 sessions, while the cost paid 593 times -- one RECORD, which is what the sentence above already said Phase 3A reads -- had no guard at all. THE GUARD IS NOW `RECORD_BUDGET_BYTES = 18432` IN bin/check-handoff (CANONICAL-ONLY, not in bin/_manifest.py), scoped to the record being written, with the full derivation beside the constant: (65,536 ceiling - 8,000 header allowance) / 3 retained receipts = 19,178 -> 18,432, leaving 2,240 B of slack. The floor of 3 is bin/tests.sh Test 34's, not the methodology's. Records have grown 3.15x: oldest 10 mean 5,478 B, newest 10 mean 17,258 B, largest ever 21,267 B (n=104, live + archives). WHY THE CEILING STAYS AND IS NOT LOWERED TO MATCH: it is what the derivation is computed FROM, and it is still the trim trigger -- `methodology_trim.py --file HANDOFFS.md --check` keys on it. Lowering it would silently re-derive the record budget downward on the next read of this note. Its source is `methodology_trim.py`'s DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES at :80 (this entry said :69 until S98; S97 flagged the drift and left it, FM #17 -- the CHANGELOG.md entry's copy of the same stale citation is UNTOUCHED and still reads :69). EXPECT THIS ENTRY TO REPORT over WHENEVER A CLOSE-OUT HAS JUST APPENDED A RECEIPT AND NO TRIM HAS RUN YET -- that is the trim trigger doing its job, not a defect; the durable question is whether the RECORD budget is green. NO max_line_bytes, deliberately and unlike the seed's SESSION_NOTES.md entry: the handoff block format is one field per line by design, so field lines run to thousands of bytes legitimately, and a per-line ceiling here would fight the format bin/check-handoff enforces rather than find a defect.

structure.why: the open-item INDEX rows, which since S99 are what this file holds — the item bodies moved to docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md and this pattern moved with them. It was ^\*\*BL-[0-9]+ —, the grep this file's header publishes; that grep now reads the DETAIL file and the header says so. The pattern is deliberately anchored on the link into the detail file, so it matches the 19 open-item rows and NOT the §Completed items pointer table beside them, which uses the same **BL-N** bold form. WHY THIS CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP: the split tripped it — the gate reported instrument-failed (worse than over, by its own ordering) the first time it ran against the new shape, which is exactly the announcement a structural instrument exists to make. Note the header's own caveat: BL-16 has no heading of its own, so it has an index row derived by hand rather than from the detail file's headings, and a count taken from the detail file is one lower than the open-item count. That is correct, not a defect.

files._: Read-mandated: SESSION_RUNNER.md Phase 0 step 3 names BACKLOG.md as the documented fallback for current priorities ('Fall back to BACKLOG.md if no repo exists'), and this fork's operational priorities live here rather than in issues (the fork has Issues disabled; they live upstream). max_bytes 65,536 is the same methodology_trim.py:69 ceiling its sibling ledgers are held to — the number BL-32, BL-36 and S89 all measured this file against. EXPECT over ON DAY ONE, 91,857 B, AND THIS IS THE POINT: S89 archived every closed item and reduced the file 33.2%, and measured that the 16 remaining OPEN items alone were 68,195 B = 1.04x the ceiling, so the residual excess is live work rather than deferred housekeeping. Closing that gap means compacting open items, which is an operator policy decision, not a session's. This entry is what turns BL-37 half (b) — adding a BACKLOG.md entry to the DISTRIBUTED seed, which needs a go-ahead — into an argument from a measurement instead of a guess. **SUPERSEDED IN PART, S99 (2026-08-18): the file is 24,638 B and the breach is CLOSED, by SPLIT rather than by the compaction this entry said would be needed.** The 18 item bodies (81,340 B) moved VERBATIM to docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md, which is read on demand and carries no ceiling — the same shape, and the same argument, as the v3.7 CLAUDE.md → docs/RELEASE_HISTORY.md extraction. Nothing was abandoned, so the operator policy question this entry raises was never reached; it stands unanswered for the day someone wants the DETAIL file smaller too. **AND THE CEILING WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE READ PATTERN BEFORE IT WAS KEPT, not assumed:** across 82 transcripts (S99's own excluded) this file was read WHOLE 23 times in 22 of them — 27% — against 584 partial reads. Its two sibling ledgers were re-derived off the whole-file axis precisely because they measured 1-in-81 (HANDOFFS.md, S98) and 1-in-80 (FRAMEWORK_LEARNINGS.md, S97); this file is read whole ~22x more often than either, so the whole-file ceiling is the right axis here and was RETAINED. Do not pattern-match the per-record/per-row remedy onto this file without re-measuring. The methodology_trim.py citation above reads :69; it is :80 as of this edit — corrected here because this sentence was being rewritten anyway, and deliberately NOT corrected in the CHANGELOG.md entry's copy of it (FM #17).

files._: DERIVED 2026-08-17 (S97), replacing the seed's 60,000 B. The old value was inherited and this key said so; what follows is the measurement that replaced it, so a successor can re-run it rather than re-argue it. MEASUREMENT: across 80 session transcripts of this repo in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-rmsharp-Development-methodology (the same corpus S90 calibrated bytes_per_token on, and the method starter-kit/context-budget.json's own SESSION_NOTES.md entry prescribes -- 'set from what your sessions ACTUALLY read'), this file was read WHOLE 1 time, read in PART 243 times, written to 18 times, and never touched at all in 47 of the 80. STATE THE UNIT: the population is TRANSCRIPTS, not sessions -- a session that compacted mid-run spans more than one file. The instrument counts TOOL CALLS, so anything the harness injects outside a tool call is invisible to it. This session's own transcript is EXCLUDED, having been caught contributing a `sed -n '1,60p'` of its own. The 1 is a FLOOR, not a point estimate: two shell range-reads (`head -30`, `sed -n '1,30p'`) are partial against today's 56 lines but may have spanned the whole table when it was shorter, so the honest range is 1-3. WHAT THAT SETTLES: a total-byte ceiling only bites when the whole file is loaded, which has happened once in 80. The cost actually paid, 243 times, is PER ROW -- a partial read returns whole rows, because a row is one physical line. So the primary guard belongs on row size, and rows have grown 4.9x: #1-#6 average 510 B, #24-#33 average 2,510 B, largest 3,451 B. WHY 65,536 AND NOT SOMETHING LARGER OR SMALLER, since the number is now doing a smaller job: (a) it is this repo's OWN ceiling for its three other accumulating ledgers, starter-kit/methodology_trim.py:80 DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES = 64 * 1024 (the CHANGELOG.md and HANDOFFS.md entries above cite it as :69, which was true when they were written -- re-derive rather than trust either); (b) a whole-file read at 65,536 B costs 23,406 tok = 55.7% of the measured 42,033-tok floor, which sits INSIDE the range of whole-file reads this repo already performs routinely -- starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md 54,363 B (46.2%) and ITERATIVE_METHODOLOGY.md 68,240 B (58.0%). This is a raise, from 50.5% to a 55.7% permitted tail, and saying so plainly is the point: it is defensible only because the read is rare AND already-routine at that size, not because the gate was inconvenient. NO max_line_bytes IS DECLARED, DELIBERATELY, and this is the one that would look like an omission. A per-row cap set anywhere useful is red on day one -- 20 of the 32 rows exceed 1,500 B -- against rows this file's own front matter forbids editing, i.e. a finding with no legal remedy. Enforcement therefore lives in bin/check-learnings (ROW_BUDGET_BYTES = 1500), scoped to rows NOT yet frozen in git HEAD, which is exactly the population a session can still act on. bin/tests.sh Test 37 pins it: 9 assertions, 4 mutants, all killed. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX -- the LEVEL. Headroom is 65,536 - 59,396 = 6,140 B, about FOUR more rows at the row budget. This session controlled the rate and deliberately did not shrink the file (FM #26/#17); the operator was shown the two shapes that do (a tighter derived ceiling forcing a shed, or a distributed archive split) and chose the rate lever. Re-open that choice when the four rows are spent, not before.

_synced: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and this is an inversion worth stating rather than an omission. The seed ships two synced entries (SESSION_RUNNER.md, SAFEGUARDS.md) that drift-check an adopter's local copy against a canonical checkout elsewhere. THIS REPO IS THAT CANONICAL. It holds no local copies to drift — starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md and starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md ARE the originals — so the naive adaptation, pointing path and canonical at the same file, would git hash-object the same blob twice and compare it to itself: an assertion of an identity that no change can falsify, which is the exact 'comment shaped like a guard' this repo has already had to delete once (Learning #16). The other half of the inversion also holds: the seed says synced files are drift-checked and never size-checked because an adopter may not edit them, so a size finding would be unactionable — here they ARE editable, so a size finding WOULD be actionable, and starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md is 52,386 B and starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md 15,386 B, both read at every adopter's Phase 0. Ceilings for them are a framework-policy decision that constrains future canonical work and would ship upstream; NOT taken here (FM #17), measured and raised instead.
_deliberate_exclusions: Measured and left out on purpose, with the numbers a future session needs: starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md 52,386 B (Phase 0 mandates it for every adopter) and starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md 15,386 B (Phase 0 step 1, 'in full, not skimmed') — both distributed, see _synced. README.md 89,175 B and ITERATIVE_METHODOLOGY.md 68,240 B — large, but read on demand and by humans, not mandated at Phase 0. docs/RELEASE_HISTORY.md — the sibling the v3.7 CLAUDE.md extraction created, read on demand. docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md 83,205 B — the sibling the S99 BACKLOG.md split created, same shape and same reason: opened only once a session knows which item it is working on. Its losslessness is proved by docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md.verify.sh, not by a ceiling. Adding any of these means declaring a ceiling nobody has defended yet, which is policy, not provisioning.
